Understanding Solar Shingle Installation & Replacement

When planning a steep-slope residential roofing project, solar shingle installation encompasses both new construction installation and the complete tear-off and replacement of aging, weathered shingles down to the structural roof decking.

Our nationwide contractor referral network connects property owners with independent, verified roofing professionals who specialize in solar systems. From architectural layout and proper ventilation integration to code-compliant fastening patterns, every project is executed to deliver optimal weatherproofing and aesthetic curb appeal.

The 5-Step Professional Installation Process

A certified residential installation follows a rigorous engineering sequence to protect your home's building envelope:

  1. Complete Tear-Off & Deck Inspection: Removal of all existing roofing layers down to bare plywood or OSB sheathing. Damaged, delaminated, or rotted decking boards are replaced with new APA-rated sheathing.
  2. Eaves & Valley Water Barrier Installation: Application of self-adhering ice-and-water membranes along critical leak zones, including eaves, valleys, rakes, and chimney saddles.
  3. Synthetic Underlayment & Metal Drip Edge: High-tear-strength synthetic underlayment is rolled horizontally across the entire deck, complemented by corrosion-resistant metal drip edge installed along all perimeter roof edges.
  4. Precision Shingle Application: Shingles are installed using manufacturer-specified nail schedules (typically 4 to 6 fasteners per shingle) to ensure wind resistance compliance up to Up to 130 MPH.
  5. Ridge Ventilation & Magnetic Cleanup: Continuous ridge exhaust vents and matching hip/ridge cap shingles are secured, followed by multiple rolling magnetic sweeps across lawns, driveways, and landscaping to collect all loose nails.

Building Code & Fire Safety Compliance

Solar Shingle Installation must meet strict building standards under the International Residential Code (IRC Chapter 9). With a certified fire rating of Class A (UL 790 certified) and an impact rating of Class 3 to 4 (Tempered solar glass), this system provides dependable defense against windborne embers, hail strikes, and severe weather events.

Independent contractors in our network pull required municipal building permits, coordinate mid-deck or final building inspections, and ensure all installations adhere to local climate amendments.

Pros and Cons of Solar Shingles

Advantages

  • Seamless roof integration: zero bulky aluminum racks or roof membrane penetrations
  • Generates clean electricity to offset rising household electric utility rates
  • Qualifies for the 30% Federal Residential Clean Energy Tax Credit (Section 25D)
  • High architectural curb appeal enhances property value and passes strict HOA reviews

Considerations & Drawbacks

  • Higher upfront investment requiring coordinated roofing and electrical trades
  • Energy generation efficiency dependent on roof azimuth (south/west orientation)
  • Dual warranties: separate coverage terms for weatherproofing roof vs electrical output

Comparing Solar to Alternative Shingle Materials

Before committing to an installation, explore how Solar compares to popular alternative roofing choices:

Asphalt Shingles

Solar shingles are frequently paired with architectural asphalt shingles on non-south-facing roof facets to balance budget and energy generation.

Metal Shingles

Both offer modern aesthetics; metal focuses purely on lifetime weather defense, while solar shingles actively pay for themselves over time.

Planning Your Solar Roofing Budget?

Installed investment for solar shingles ranges from $2,100 – $3,800 per square (before tax credits). Pricing factors include roof square footage, slope pitch complexity, tear-off layer disposal, and plywood deck repairs.

Frequently Asked Questions About Solar Shingle Installation

How do solar shingles differ from traditional rooftop solar panels?

Traditional solar panels are mounted on aluminum racks bolted through your existing roof shingles. Solar shingles are the roof itself: they serve as both primary waterproof building shingles and electricity-generating photovoltaic tiles, sitting flush with the roofline.

Do solar shingles qualify for the Federal Solar Tax Credit?

Yes. Qualifying residential solar shingle installations qualify for the 30% Federal Residential Clean Energy Credit (IRC Section 25D) on both solar hardware and associated electrical installation costs. Consult your CPA for tax guidance.

Can you combine solar shingles with regular shingles?

Yes. Most solar shingle installations install active photovoltaic shingles on sunny south- and west-facing roof slopes, while matching architectural or composite shingles are installed on shaded north-facing facets to maximize return on investment.
